title: LLM-Driven Autonomous Vehicles Inherit Human Driver Biases in Pedestrian Yielding: Results and Implications From A New Benchmark
measurement_description: The paper measured whether Large Language Models (LLMs) and Vision-Language Models (VLMs) acting as autonomous vehicle (AV) driving assistants exhibit biases by comparing their pedestrian-yielding decisions (whether to stop or continue). Specifically, it evaluated whether models changed their stop rates based on the pedestrian's injected or perceived demographic characteristics, including religion.
findings: The study found that GPT-4o exhibited small but statistically significant bias in its AV pedestrian-yielding decisions based on religion. It yielded significantly less often to "Muslim", "Christian", and "Sikh" pedestrians compared to "Jewish" pedestrians.
